title: Home Mortgage Loans: when a loan becomes delinquent and how it returns to active
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: when a loan becomes delinquent and how it returns to active

This policy governs the delinquency status of Home Mortgage Loans loans: when an active loan becomes delinquent and when a delinquent loan returns to active.

## Policy clauses

1. **Becoming delinquent.** The loan becomes delinquent when an installment is unpaid 30 days after its due date. The basis is the bank's record of that loan's days past due.
2. **Cure.** A delinquent loan returns to active once every past-due installment is paid, meaning all past-due installments and escrow.
3. **Outside this policy.** Foreclosure, short sale and deed-in-lieu decisions are outside this policy.

## Status table

| Loan situation | Status |
|---|---|
| Installment paid, or unpaid fewer than 30 days after its due date | Stays active |
| Installment unpaid 30 days after its due date | Becomes delinquent |
| Delinquent, some past-due installments still unpaid | Stays delinquent |
| Delinquent, every past-due installment paid | Returns to active |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical loan, installment due 1 March)

| Days past due on the loan's record | Status |
|---|---|
| 29 | Active; the installment is not yet unpaid 30 days after its due date |
| 30 | Delinquent |

## Cure example (hypothetical)

A delinquent loan has two past-due installments, due 1 April and 1 May.

- The borrower pays the 1 April installment only: one past-due installment remains, so the loan stays delinquent.
- The borrower then pays the 1 May installment as well: every past-due installment is paid, so the loan returns to active.

## Basis Q&A

- **Does paying the most recent installment alone cure the loan?** No. Every past-due installment must be paid.
- **Does the agent decide on foreclosure, short sale or deed-in-lieu?** Those decisions are outside this policy.
